tasks.short: Track frame and lens stock, total daily sales, fill insurer claims, check them, submit them, and do simple bookkeeping.

steps.what: Optician tracks inventory of frames and lenses in a spreadsheet
Optician scans the frame's barcode at the sale, which books it out of stock
Optician tracks sales by totalling the day's till receipts
Optician fills patient insurance information on insurer claim forms
Optician checks the final claims before submission: customer, insured items and amounts against the sale and prescription, and the insurer each claim goes to
Optician submits patient insurance information in insurers' portals
Optician performs simple bookkeeping of takings and expenses: by typing in a spreadsheet today, by booking only the exceptions the rules leave after the change
Optician checks the bookings the rules propose: amounts, expense types and accounts against the takings and the bank lines
Optician posts the checked bookings to the bookkeeping

tasks.design: Frames carry barcodes, so each sale books stock out in the shop system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) and the stock list is not kept in a spreadsheet; the day's sales report replaces totalling receipts. Claims are built from the sale, the prescription and the customer's insurance details in the shop system. Once checked, claims for insurers that take standard electronic claims, about 70%, go out as messages; the rest are still entered in insurers' portals. Till takings and the bank feed come into the bookkeeping ({ERP}) as bookings proposed by rules per expense type; the optician books the exceptions, checks the proposed bookings and posts them once.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stock, sales and books were kept in spreadsheets and claims typed per insurer.
tasks.enabler_now: Shop systems book stock by sale and send standard insurer claims.
tasks.still_hard: Insurers with their own portals still need typing.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining to a customer what their insurer will pay.
tasks.altitude: The optician checks claims and books instead of typing them.

evidence.claim: Optical shop systems can book stock by sale and send standard electronic claims to insurers.
Prescriptions and insurance details are health data, special category under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from the day's sales to the books updated; annual accounts are outside.
Input contract: frames barcoded and insurer links set up; fallback is spreadsheets and portals.
Scenario: about 70% of claims go to insurers that take standard electronic claims.

The optician checks every claim before it goes, and checks the proposed bookings before posting them; scanning at the sale, both checks and the posting keep their full time. s1 keeps 30 for frames without barcodes and lenses; s3 keeps 40 for completing claims; s5 keeps 30 for portal claims; s6 keeps 30 for the exceptions.

incremental.description: Optician corrects stock after spot counts.

approvals.approved_version: Each claim with customer, insured items and amounts exactly as checked by the optician in s4, submitted once to the customer's insurer, as a standard electronic message or in that insurer's portal; any change needs a new check.
The day's bookings with amounts, expense types and accounts exactly as checked by the optician in s6b, posted once to the shop's bookkeeping; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of claims still go through portals and many frames lack barcodes, so s1, s3 and s5 keep 60 (47.2); high: about 70% of claims electronic as assumed (62.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Fit the glasses and show the client how to wear them, explain care and cleaning, give a care card, and answer follow-up calls.

steps.what: Optician instructs clients in how to wear new eyeglasses while fitting them
Optician explains how to care for and clean the eyeglasses
Optician writes care notes for the client by hand
Optician answers clients' follow-up calls about getting used to the glasses

tasks.design: A care card per lens type, for example progressive or contact lenses, is printed from the shop system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) with the client's lens details, so care notes are not written by hand. Fitting, explaining and answering calls stay with the optician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Care notes were written by hand when needed.
tasks.enabler_now: Shop systems print standard cards filled with the client's details.
tasks.still_hard: Clients new to progressive lenses need time and patience.
tasks.human_edge: Helping an older client get used to progressive lenses.

reach.learn: Whether the card helps at home.

evidence.claim: Shop systems can print standard care cards filled with the client's lens details.

assumptions: Boundary: from the glasses ready to questions answered; refraction is outside.
Input contract: care cards set up per lens type; fallback is handwriting.
Fitting, explaining and answering calls keep their full time. s3 keeps 40 for printing the card and adding a client-specific note; the card is a standard leaflet per lens type.

incremental.description: Optician keeps care cards current per lens type.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many clients need notes the standard cards do not cover, so s3 keeps 70 (1.0); high: cards cover most lens types (2.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Demonstrate and supervise students with clients, give feedback, sign off competences, write progress reports for the school, and plan students' shifts.

steps.what: Optician supervises the training of student opticians with clients
Optician gives students feedback on their work
Optician signs off competences in the student's paper portfolio
Optician writes progress reports for the school
Optician checks the final progress report: the assessment matches the student's signed-off competences and the feedback given, and it goes to the right school and student
Optician submits the checked progress report to the school's e-portfolio
Optician plans students' shifts in a spreadsheet

tasks.design: Competences are signed off on a tablet in the school's e-portfolio ({LMS}) instead of the paper portfolio, which takes the same time. The progress report form there opens with the signed-off competences; the optician writes the assessment, checks the report and submits it once. Students' shifts are added to the shop roster ({OTHER}) instead of a separate spreadsheet. Supervising and giving feedback stay with the optician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Portfolios were on paper and reports written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: School e-portfolios take sign-offs and report forms from workplaces.
tasks.still_hard: Each school uses its own portfolio.
tasks.human_edge: Letting a student handle a difficult client and stepping in at the right moment.

evidence.claim: School e-portfolios can take competence sign-offs and progress forms from workplace supervisors.

assumptions: Boundary: from the student on shift to shifts planned; the school's assessment is outside.
Input contract: the school gives access to its e-portfolio; fallback is paper.

Supervising, feedback, signing off, the report check and the submit keep their full time. s4 keeps 80 because only the list of competences fills in; s5 keeps 50 because shifts go straight into the roster instead of a spreadsheet and then the roster.
research_questions: Do schools get reports on time more often?

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep: learning a school's e-portfolio is a one-off.

approvals.approved_version: The progress report with its assessment exactly as checked by the optician in s4b, submitted once to this student's file in the school's e-portfolio; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the student's school keeps paper portfolios, so the report form does not fill and s4 keeps 100 (2.5); high: the school uses an e-portfolio (5.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Choose frames for the collection, meet supplier reps, reorder sold frames, order lenses per customer job, check orders, send them, and check deliveries.

steps.what: Optician decides which frames to buy for the collection
Optician meets supplier representatives to purchase frames
Optician checks stock to reorder sold frames
Optician orders lenses for each customer job
Optician checks the final frame reorders: models, colours, sizes, quantities and the supplier
Optician sends the checked frame reorders to the frame suppliers: by e-mail or phone today, through the supplier link or by e-mail after the change
Optician checks the final lens orders: each customer's prescription, lens type, coatings and the lab it goes to
Optician sends the checked lens orders to the lens labs: by e-mail or phone today, through the lab link or by e-mail after the change
Optician checks deliveries against the orders

tasks.design: The shop system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) lists sold frames for reorder from the day's sales, so stock is not checked by hand. Lens orders fill from the customer job. The optician checks frame reorders and lens orders separately and sends each once; for linked lens labs and suppliers, about 70% of orders, they go through the integration, and the rest are still e-mailed or phoned. Choosing the collection, meeting reps and checking deliveries stay with the optician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reorders were found by checking stock and lens orders typed or phoned in.
tasks.enabler_now: Shop systems list reorders from sales and send lens orders to linked labs.
tasks.still_hard: Small suppliers and labs have no ordering link.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing frames that suit the shop's customers.

evidence.claim: Optical shop systems can list reorders from sales and send lens orders to linked labs.

assumptions: Boundary: from the season ahead to deliveries checked; paying invoices is outside.
Input contract: supplier and lab links set up; fallback is e-mail and phone.
Scenario: about 70% of orders go to linked labs and suppliers.

The optician checks every frame reorder and lens order before it goes; both checks keep their full time. s3 keeps 40 for reviewing the reorder list; s4 keeps 40 for completing lens orders; s6 and s6f keep 30 for orders still e-mailed or phoned.

incremental.description: Optician resolves orders the lab link rejects.

approvals.approved_version: Each lens order with customer job, prescription, lens type and coatings exactly as checked by the optician in s5, sent once to the named lens lab through the link or by e-mail; any change needs a new check.

The frame reorder with models, colours, sizes and quantities exactly as checked by the optician in s5f, sent once to the named frame supplier through the link or by e-mail; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of orders go to unlinked labs and suppliers, so s4, s6 and s6f keep 60 (22.5); high: about 70% linked as assumed (30.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The optician keeps fitting glasses, training students, choosing frames and checking claims; spreadsheet stock, typed claims, handwritten care notes and phoned orders shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An optician with more time with clients.
